name: AWS EC2 G6 / G6e (NVIDIA L4 and L40S, inference-optimized)
region: us-east-1, us-west-2 and most commercial regions
price_basis: per GPU-hour. g6.48xlarge = 8x L4 at $13.3504/instance-hr / 8 = $1.6688. g6e.48xlarge = 8x L40S at $30.13118/8 = $3.7664. g5.48xlarge = 8x A10G at $16.288/8 = $2.036. Single-GPU g6.xlarge = 1x L4 at $0.8048. Fetched 2026-10-03 from the 2026-09-25 offer file; no regional variation found. notes:
THE PRACTICAL INFERENCE FAMILIES on AWS, and the only ones here actually in stock - unlike every p5 record, no $0.00 sentinel appears for g6/g6e and both regions publish real rates. L4 at $1.67/GPU-hr with 24GB is the answer for a small-to-mid model that wants HBM-class bandwidth without Hopper pricing; L40S at $3.77 is the Ada step up with 48GB for models that do not fit. Single-GPU shapes exist and are the sane starting point. Spot applies and AWS advertises up to 90% off on-demand, but I could NOT retrieve a concrete spot rate for these SKUs: the per-instance-type spot table renders client-side and spot-price.s3.amazonaws.com returned HTTP 403. No spot number is recorded here rather than guessing - query describe-spot-price-history before relying on one. AWS's 'up to 40% savings on DL training and HPC infrastructure costs' versus the previous GPU generation is a vendor claim.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04): the accelerator in this instance family sits BELOW the ECCN 3A090.a thresholds - TPP and performance density for this class are under the >= 4800 / >= 5.92 boundary - so the advanced-computing licence regime with its case-by-case and D:5 screening does not attach to the die. Recorded false for that reason, NOT because the part is unregulated: it remains under the EAR and subject to destination-country import rules and to consignee/ultimate-parent screening against the Entity, Unverified and MEU lists under 15 CFR part 744, and a complete system containing it can still be controlled. The practical effect is that L4/L40S/A10 capacity is materially easier to serve to a wide set of destinations than H100-class capacity, which is part of why its price band sits where it does. Source: spl-eccn-3a090-ccl.

 LEAD TIME: null, and correct as null. For a listed on-demand instance type the provisioning delay is effectively zero - capacity is allocated per request - so a week count would be meaningless; the real gate for scarce shapes is either a quota increase or a capacity reservation, not a lead time. Where a published commitment horizon exists it IS recorded: AWS documents that a Capacity Block may be reserved with a start time up to EIGHT WEEKS in the future (source spl-aws-capacity-block-booking-horizon), which is a floor on how far ahead scarce capacity must be committed, not a wait. On-demand and Spot tiers publish no lead time at all; their constraint is availability, and the repo records that as availability=in-stock or a spot/reality note rather than as a fabricated week figure. Probe log in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.
export_control_regime: EAR 3A001 or EAR99 (below the 3A090.a TPP / performance-density thresholds) + EAR 744.23 (Entity List) + EAR 744.6 (Unverified / MEU lists)
export_control_note: MECHANISM: the part falls BELOW the ECCN 3A090.a/.b TPP and performance-density thresholds, so the advanced-computing licence regime, its case-by-case China/Macau carve-out and its D:5 screening do NOT attach. What remains is the general EAR plus destination-country import rules and screening of the consignee and its ultimate parent against the Entity, Unverified and MEU lists. NO LICENCE REQUIRED for the sale itself; the screening is a party-listing check, not a performance-threshold check. The binding ECCN determination for any specific part is the exporter's own classification, not this record.
lead_time_basis: lead_time_weeks is null because the quantity is structurally not applicable: on-demand cloud capacity starts on request, so there is no order-to-delivery lead time. The constraint is the price per GPU-hour and the availability snapshot, not an interval. The one caveat worth keeping: scarce tiers gate capacity behind a reservation or Capacity Block commitment (AWS caps the booking horizon at 8 weeks, source spl-aws-capacity-block-booking-horizon), and that is a commitment window, not a lead time.
